newsitem.title: UK: UK's George says Euro growth needed for EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK's George says Euro growth needed for EMU.

text.p: The Governor of the Bank of England said in an interview broadcast on Sunday that it would be more difficult for a single European currency to go ahead without a pick-up in economic growth in Europe.
Eddie George said it was important that Britain should meet the conditions for joining the single currency in January 1999, whether the decision is to join or stay out.

"I think it will make a very big difference whether the European economy as a whole, which has been going through a very sluggish period, actually picks up pace between now and the end of 1997 and early 1998 when the decision has to be taken.
"Without that then I think it would be much more difficult for the preconditions to be met and therefore the decision to go ahead to be taken," he told BBC-2 television's Money Programme.
George said the decision on whether to join the single currency was a political matter, but it would be wrong to come to premature conclusions.

"It's not a decision for me -- it's a political decision -- the politicians see it that they will look at the circumstances -- I think that's entirely right -- I think it would be unwise to prejudge...," he said.

But he added: "I regard it as absolutely fundamental that Britain should be ready on January 1, 1999 to prosper whether the decision is that we should join or whether the decision is that we should stay out and I am quite determined that we will be in that position."
George issued a warning against European countries making a one-off effort to join the single curreny and then reverting to spendthrift ways.

"I think it would be immensely dangerous not just for the country that got under the wire but for the other countries who were in the monetary union and I think those countries will be extremely sensitive to that risk," he said.
George rejected suggestions that the introduction of a single currency would threaten London's pre-eminence as a financial centre.

"I don't believe that the position of London depends in a fundamental sense on the currency in which London operates -- London is not London because of sterling -- London is London because of the strengths of the financial institutions here," the governor said. -- London newsroom 0171-542-7717
